currentStage: Phase 4D — Visual direction, responsive composition and candidate promotion
activeStage: Three lanes are open. Phase 4D.8/4D.9 — the visual review verdict on the genuine-business candidate set — is unchanged and still outstanding: the machinery is built, the evidence is captured, and no candidate is promoted. Phase 4.2A — the static/content renderer — is implemented, re-anchored on current main and evidenced, and its own independent visual review of the statically rendered nbm output has not been issued. 4D.2 landed beside both: a person can now supply the design references those decisions are partly about.
outstandingProductGates: phase-4d-visual-review-verdict: the nbm candidate set is generated, built and photographed, and no candidate is promoted. The factory created them, so the factory cannot promote one. The evidence is now reviewer-reachable rather than buried in build output: `npm run acceptance:visual-candidates` leaves durable factory state at .app-builder/visual-review, `npm run review:visual-candidates` opens the ordinary Builder Console over exactly that state, and the stage's compare view shows both candidates at three widths over six routes with the differing axes, the responsive plan, every DesignLint finding, the frozen truth, the refused direction and the scoped critic criteria. A reviewer who did not create them still has to pass, rework or reject each candidate against those criteria before Phase 4D closes.

phase-4-2a-static-visual-review: the genuine nbm business now renders through the static/content renderer. It generates, installs, checks and builds as an independent repository with zero client JavaScript and six route documents against the application renderer's 218,118 bytes and one; it presents by the same promoted visual direction, carries the same shell classes and compiled tokens, passes DesignLint 0/0/0 and axe WCAG 2.1 A/AA at desktop and mobile, and is photographed at three widths over six routes plus the enquiry-failure state. `npm run acceptance:static-renderer` leaves that evidence at .app-builder/static-renderer and stops. What is outstanding is the same thing 4D is waiting on and for the same reason: the creator of a rendering may not pass its own visual review. A reviewer who did not produce it has to look at the captures and say whether the static nbm site is at least as good as the application-rendered one before 4.2A closes.

bespoke-presentation-fulfilment: a failed visual review whose criterion no art-direction axis can answer now classifies a customPresentation requirement — the section, the art-direction need, why the registry is insufficient, the required responsive and motion behaviour, and the owner. Nothing fulfils one yet. The Presentation Registry has stopped being allowed to answer 'the closest existing component', and until an implementation lane exists a classified requirement is a recorded gap rather than a build. docs/VISUAL_EXCELLENCE.md §9 carries it as the row it blocks.
nextStage: Phase 4D.8/4D.9. The Factory can now produce several genuinely different presentations of one frozen product truth and decide between them. 4D.1 made promotion a recorded decision with a deterministic gate: a DesignLint violation blocks promotion outright, a warning reaches review but the reviewer must speak to it by rule, a recommendation never blocks, exactly one candidate is promoted and the creator cannot promote its own. 4D.4 made asset readiness an art-direction input, so an imagery-led direction is refused before it becomes a page of grey rectangles. 4D.5 added a ResponsiveCompositionPlan subordinate to the ArtDirectionPlan, with mobile content order, navigation treatment, hero stacking, density and motion all read by the template. 4D.6 added four visual directions differing structurally rather than thematically, with a diversity check over three planes that refuses a theme swap before it costs an evidence capture. 4D.7 captures comparable evidence per candidate from its own built output. The nbm genuine-business run generated two candidates over one truth, refused the imagery-led direction with a recorded reason, built and photographed both at three widths across six routes, and both lint clean. What remains is a verdict from someone who did not create them, and then promotion. 4D.2, 4D.3 and the comparison canvas are recorded in deferredCapabilities. Automated cross-provider visual judgement remains unexecuted and is recorded as such rather than simulated. 4D.2 is no longer deferred: a project can supply design references, so the condition that deferred it — a supplied screenshot, moodboard or approved reference URL AND a direction-selection decision asset readiness and project type cannot make — is met by a real supplier and a real consumer. Approved adopt/avoid traits refuse a direction on a structural axis and tune the ArtDirectionPlan's intent on a scaled one, before compileArtDirectionPlan runs, so restraint still clamps them. The visual review now scores every criterion against gates.visual in config/agent-pipelines.json, a below-bar verdict cannot be recorded as a pass, and a set with no winner can be sent back for one bounded, targeted rework pass with lineage or rejected outright. What remains outstanding is unchanged: who issues the verdict. Beside it, Phase 4.2A gave the factory a second architectural output, re-anchored on this main rather than the one it forked from: a project type now selects a renderer and the renderer names its template, deterministically from the project type and the enabled modules alone. Marketing and content sites are rendered statically by a pinned Astro template; SaaS, consumer, internal and AI projects are unchanged on the React/Vite template, and a capability override only ever moves a project towards a fuller client runtime, never away from one. The two renderers share one presentation contract, one design system source and one element-identity derivation, so the promoted art direction, the ResponsiveCompositionPlan and the MotionContract survive a renderer change rather than being re-decided. Five reusable factory defects the static renderer exposed were fixed at their cause: a lint step that silently linted nothing in every generated project, a preview reported as running before it could serve, the Console serving its own module graph into preview frames, a dev-only diagnostics block distorting every rendered-evidence capture, and an SPA catch-all baked into the deployment adapter. 4.2B icons, 4.2C Pagefind, 4.2D typed structured data and 4.2E deterministic OG imagery are deliberately not started: each needs a real consumer first. docs/PHASE_4_2_EXECUTION.md records the measurements, the adoption reasoning and the one known limitation. What 4.2A is waiting on is what 4D is waiting on, and for the same reason: a reviewer who did not produce the rendering.

deferredCapabilities.title: Deterministic design-intelligence catalogue
deferredCapabilities.reason: No component asks "which reviewed design patterns fit this project?". BrandSpec reads the knowledge pack's own brand observations, ArtDirectionPlan reads config/layout-patterns.json, and the Presentation Registry is compiled from what the template renders. A catalogue built now would have one producer and no reader.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A real 4D consumer cannot answer a project/industry/intent pattern question from deterministic config. Then document that consumer first, and implement only the smallest lexical (BM25/keyword) catalogue it needs — no vector store, no embeddings, no generic design corpus.

deferredCapabilities.title: MessagingPlan
deferredCapabilities.reason: The composition already carries what a MessagingPlan would organise, with provenance. Page narrative is the section sequence; CTA strategy is derived from the declared conversion goals; proof requirements and their gaps are `declaredProofGap`; audience is on the manifest; forbidden claims are the existing source/provenance boundary. A second narrative authority would have fields nothing reads and a second place the same decision could be made.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: An art-direction or composition decision needs narrative information the composition cannot express — a proof sequence that does not follow from what is available, or an objection-handling order. Implement only the fields that decision reads.

deferredCapabilities.title: Visual comparison canvas
deferredCapabilities.reason: The ordinary Builder Console does the comparison. Its candidate panel shows every candidate side by side, switches route and viewport over the captured evidence, names the axes that actually differ rather than leaving them to be spotted, shows the responsive plan field by field, shows what the deterministic checks settled and what the reviewer must speak to, exposes the scoped critic criteria, and promotes exactly one. The one usability failure found was the 330px activity sidebar cropping two full-page captures into roughly 150px columns; the panel moved to the builder stage and the problem went with it. The failing surface was the narrow column, not the Console, so tldraw or an equivalent would still be a dependency bought against a layout problem.
deferredCapabilities.revivesWhen: A concrete comparison task proves the Console cannot do it — spatial arrangement of many more candidates, or freehand annotation a reviewer genuinely needs to hand back. Record the task first.
